text.p: Israel's Jaf-Ora Ltd will acquire a stake in Elite Industries Ltd buttressing a move by the Federman group to dissolve shared control of Elite with Gideon Holdings, a Jaf-Ora spokesman said on Sunday.

The spokesman confirmed newspaper reports this morning that the Jaf-Ora acquisition would be financed through loans. Newspapers said Jaf-Ora, a soft drinks concern, envisaged eventually also buying the Federman group's holding in Elite.
Jaf-Ora's announcement comes after the Federman group said on Thursday it had triggered a "Buy Me, Buy You" agreement it has Gideon Holdings, Elite's second-biggest shareholder, to buy out Gideon.
The terms of agreement require Gideon, which is controlled by the Strauss family, to accept the offer or to buy out the Federman group at a 2.5 percent discount.

Under the agreement the Federman group reached with Jaf-Ora, should Strauss agree to sell its Elite holding Jaf-Ora will buy it, the spokesman said. If Strauss opts to buy the Federman holding, the spokesman said, Jaf-Ora would be compensated for the costs of making the offer.
Jaf-Ora is 64 percent-owned by Israel Cold Storage Supply Co and 26 percent by Clal Industries.
The Strauss family, which owns Strauss Dairies, holds at least 17.5 percent of equity and 19.1 percent of voting rights in Elite.
The spokesman said Jaf-Ora would pay approximately $58 million for the holding, valuing Elite at more than $330 million against its Tel Aviv stock market valuation of $244 million as of Thursday.
Federman has offered to pay Gideon 38 shekels ($11.28) for every Elite 1 ordinary share it has and 67.25 shekels for every par 5 ordinary share for a total of $66 million.
Israel's Globes business newspaper said Federman and Strauss wanted to dissolve their joint control of the company because they were at loggerheads over managerial and strategic issues.

The Federman group has a 13 percent equity holding, which gives its voting rights equal to 26.28 percent. Globes said the shares were collateral for loans of more than $20 million the family used to buy the holdings of the British commodities firm ED&F Man in Elite early last year.
The family, which is led by David Federman, Elite's chairman, turned around shortly after buying the Man shares and sold 15 percent of Elite to the Strauss family.
Elite has undergone far-reaching changes since the Strauss family came on the scene. Much of the company's loss-making European businesses, acquired in 1992, have been closed or sold off.
